exercises.name: Easy walking / light cycling
exercises.how: Walk at a relaxed pace, gradually increasing to a comfortable brisk pace for a warm-up. Swing arms naturally, keep gaze ahead and breathe easily. For a cool-down, gradually slow the pace. Easy cycling can substitute before/after gym.
exercises.watch: Do not force jogging. Stop for dizziness, unusual breathlessness or symptoms that worsen with movement.
exercises.why: Particularly relevant because Ryan reports that walking often eases his back symptoms. Also forms the safe base of sport warm-ups.
exercises.alternatives: E21 marching on the spot; brief corridor walk; easy stationary cycling.

exercises.name: Supine pelvic tilts
exercises.how: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet supported. Gently flatten the lower back towards the mat by tipping the pelvis backwards, then release to neutral. Use a small, controlled motion and keep breathing.
exercises.watch: No forceful arching, breath-holding or pushing through sharp pain.
exercises.why: Gentle, low-load movement when stiff after rest.
exercises.alternatives: E10 sit-to-stand or E01 walking if lying down is uncomfortable.

exercises.name: Supine knee rolls
exercises.how: Lie on your back, knees bent and feet together or hip-width. Slowly let both knees tip a short distance to one side while shoulders remain relaxed; return to centre and repeat on the other side.
exercises.watch: Keep range small; do not wrench the knees towards the floor or allow a painful spinal twist.
exercises.why: Comfortable movement in the low back and hips.
exercises.alternatives: E02 pelvic tilts if rotation is provocative.

exercises.name: Cat-camel (gentle)
exercises.how: On hands and knees with hands under shoulders and knees under hips, slowly round the back a little and then return towards a gentle, comfortable arch. Keep neck in line with the trunk rather than looking up sharply.
exercises.watch: Avoid large end ranges; **skip if pressure through the shoulder, wrist or neck is uncomfortable**.
exercises.why: Gentle controlled spinal movement.
exercises.alternatives: E02 pelvic tilts; seated small back movement if recommended by physio.

photo.note: Two-position cat–cow photograph; use a smaller range

exercises.name: Gentle chin retractions (chin tucks)
exercises.how: Sit or stand tall with eyes level. Glide the head gently straight backwards as though making a small double chin, without looking down or tilting back. Relax fully between reps.
exercises.watch: Do not jam the chin in, lift the chin or push into a headache, arm tingling or dizziness.
exercises.why: Small, controlled neck movement for desk time and daily mobility.
exercises.alternatives: E06 gentle rotations or simply a change of position if this aggravates symptoms.

exercises.name: Gentle neck rotations
exercises.how: Keep shoulders relaxed and look slowly to the left, return to centre, then right. Stop before pain or pulling becomes strong.
exercises.watch: No hand assistance, quick turns, head circles or forced end-range stretches.
exercises.why: Maintain comfortable neck movement.
exercises.alternatives: Smaller turns; stop this movement if it causes dizziness or neurological symptoms.

exercises.name: Shoulder blade setting
exercises.how: Standing or sitting upright, let the shoulders relax down. Very gently draw the shoulder blades towards each other, then fully release. Arms remain relaxed near the sides.
exercises.watch: No forceful pinching, shoulder shrugging or pain in the frozen shoulder.
exercises.why: Short break from sustained desk posture; gentle shoulder-girdle movement.
exercises.alternatives: Shoulder relaxation and easy walking.

exercises.name: Supported shoulder pendulum
exercises.how: Support yourself securely with the unaffected arm. Hinge forward only a little from the hips if your back allows, let the affected arm hang and make tiny relaxed movements or circles by moving the body, not by actively swinging the shoulder.
exercises.watch: Back pain from leaning or shoulder pain from movement. Skip if either occurs. Do not swing vigorously.
exercises.why: A commonly used gentle shoulder mobility exercise; does not replace a tailored frozen-shoulder programme.
exercises.alternatives: E07 shoulder blade setting.

exercises.name: Wall-assisted shoulder slide
exercises.how: Face a wall, place the fingers of the affected hand against it and walk the fingers slowly upwards only to a gentle, approved range. Lower with control. Keep shoulder relaxed and do not arch the lower back.
exercises.watch: Sharp shoulder pain, hiking the shoulder or compensating through the neck/back. No forced overhead range.
exercises.why: Optional shoulder mobility progress once the physio confirms it is appropriate.
exercises.alternatives: E08 pendulum; clinician's prescribed assisted movement.

photo.note: Finger walk up wall; clinician review first

exercises.name: Sit-to-stand
exercises.how: Place feet about hip-width, lean forwards slightly from the hips, stand up smoothly and sit back down under control. Use hands for assistance if needed.
exercises.watch: Avoid collapsing into the chair, painful knee angles or hard bracing through the neck.
exercises.why: Practical movement break and light leg activity.
exercises.alternatives: E21 march on the spot.

exercises.name: Standing split-stance hip-flexor stretch
exercises.how: Take a small staggered stance, back heel lifted. Gently tuck the pelvis, tighten the back-leg glute and shift your weight forward a little until you feel a mild stretch at the front of the back hip. Stay tall.
exercises.watch: Do not arch the lower back or push into groin pain.
exercises.why: Optional flexibility for long periods spent sitting.
exercises.alternatives: Shorter stance; skip if back discomfort increases.

exercises.name: Wall calf stretch
exercises.how: Hands lightly on wall, step one foot back, keep back heel down and knee gently straight, then lean forward slightly until the calf stretches. Repeat on the other side.
exercises.watch: Do not bounce or force the ankle.
exercises.why: Useful after tennis footwork and walking.
exercises.alternatives: E20 calf raises as dynamic ankle movement (not an identical stretch).

exercises.name: Supine hamstring stretch, with strap if useful
exercises.how: Lie on your back with one knee bent and foot on the floor. Lift the other thigh using a strap behind the thigh or foot, keeping a **slight bend** in that knee. Raise only until a gentle stretch is felt at the back of the thigh. Keep lower back relaxed.
exercises.watch: Do not straighten the knee aggressively or pull the foot towards you. Stop for shooting pain, tingling or symptoms down the leg (which may not be a simple muscle stretch).
exercises.why: Requested optional hamstring mobility, without unsupported toe-touching.
exercises.alternatives: Gentle seated hamstring stretch if recommended by physio; otherwise skip.

exercises.name: Supine figure-four glute stretch
exercises.how: Lie on your back, place one ankle on the opposite thigh just above the knee. If comfortable, draw the supporting thigh gently towards you to feel a mild stretch in the buttock.
exercises.watch: No force on the knee; stop for radiating nerve-like symptoms or aggravated back pain.
exercises.why: Optional gluteal and hip mobility after activity.
exercises.alternatives: Easy walking; E11 hip-flexor stretch (targets a different region).

exercises.name: Glute bridge
exercises.how: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet hip-width. Exhale gently, tighten the buttocks and lift hips a modest amount while keeping ribs relaxed. Lower slowly.
exercises.watch: Do not hyperextend the lower back, push through the neck or hold your breath. Stop if it increases spinal pain.
exercises.why: Low-load gluteal strengthening and hip control.
exercises.alternatives: E10 sit-to-stand or E17 clamshell if comfortable.

exercises.name: Supine abdominal march
exercises.defaultDose: 6 lifts per side; R09 may use 2 sets.
exercises.how: Lie on your back, knees bent and feet supported. Keep spine in a comfortable neutral position and lightly tighten the abdomen. Slowly lift one foot a few centimetres, set it down, then change legs. Breathe steadily.
exercises.watch: No back arching, hard abdominal bracing, neck straining or breath-holding. If this is too much, slide one heel a short distance along the mat instead.
exercises.why: Gentle trunk control without shoulder weight-bearing.
exercises.alternatives: Supine heel slide (simpler variation); walking.

exercises.name: Side-lying clamshell
exercises.defaultDose: 8 each side; R09 may use 2 sets.
exercises.how: Lie on one side with hips and knees gently bent, feet together and head supported. Keeping pelvis still, raise the upper knee a little without separating the feet. Lower slowly, then change sides.
exercises.watch: Do not roll the pelvis backwards or strain the shoulder supporting the body; rest the head on a pillow/arm comfortably.
exercises.why: Gentle outer-hip strengthening relevant to walking, stairs and tennis movement.
exercises.alternatives: E10 sit-to-stand if side-lying is uncomfortable.

exercises.name: Standing hip hinge rehearsal
exercises.how: Stand with soft knees and hands resting on hips. Push hips backwards a short distance while torso inclines forwards as one unit; return by pushing through the feet and gently squeezing glutes. Keep neck in line with torso.
exercises.watch: No rounded/forced back, painful forward bend or heavy weight. Use a very small range at first.
exercises.why: Practise a basic movement pattern before gym and after desk work.
exercises.alternatives: E10 sit-to-stand.

exercises.name: Mini bodyweight squat
exercises.how: Feet comfortable width apart; bend hips and knees to a shallow, comfortable depth, then stand. Keep knees tracking towards toes and chest comfortably upright.
exercises.watch: No deep squat requirement, loaded barbell or breath-holding. Stop if back or knees complain.
exercises.why: Progressive preparation for footwork and leg exercise.
exercises.alternatives: E10 sit-to-stand.

exercises.name: Calf raises
exercises.how: Stand tall, lightly hold a support, slowly rise onto the balls of the feet and lower again.
exercises.watch: Do not bounce; keep stable.
exercises.why: Gentle lower-leg activation before tennis.
exercises.alternatives: E26 ankle rocks.

exercises.name: Marching on the spot
exercises.how: March easily on the spot, gradually raising the knees a little higher if comfortable. Natural arm movements; relax shoulders.
exercises.watch: Avoid vigorous bouncing if uncomfortable or dizzy.
exercises.why: Gradually raise heart rate without complex movement.
exercises.alternatives: E01 walking.

exercises.name: Gentle side shuffle
exercises.equipment: A few metres of safe space
exercises.how: In a relaxed athletic stance, take a few small side steps to the right and back to the left. Keep feet apart and movements controlled; start at a fraction of match speed.
exercises.watch: Avoid rapid, explosive changes of direction, twisting the back or turning the head abruptly.
exercises.why: Tennis-specific lateral movement preparation.
exercises.alternatives: Slow side-stepping without a shuffle.

exercises.name: Supported front-back leg swings
exercises.how: Hold a secure support, stand tall and swing one leg forwards and backwards over a short, pain-free arc. Keep torso as still as practical; change legs.
exercises.watch: No jerking, full-range kicking or excessive arching through the back.
exercises.why: Prepare hips for on-court movement.
exercises.alternatives: E21 marching.

exercises.name: Shallow lateral lunge
exercises.how: Step a comfortable distance sideways, bend the stepping knee slightly and shift hips back a little. Push back to standing and alternate sides.
exercises.watch: Do not descend deeply or twist the knee/back. Use wall support if balance requires it.
exercises.why: Rehearse side-to-side movement for tennis.
exercises.alternatives: E22 gentle side-steps.

photo.note: Side lunge; use a shallower depth than pictured

exercises.name: Progressive short-court rally
exercises.how: Begin with very gentle short-court hitting using compact forehands and backhands, then gradually increase movement and stroke pace within a comfortable range.
exercises.watch: No explosive serving, overhead shots, hard rotation or pain-provoking neck/shoulder mechanics. Stop if symptoms develop. If tennis is not cleared, skip this movement rather than replacing it with risky hitting.
exercises.why: Gradual transition from general warm-up to actual tennis movement.
exercises.alternatives: Easy shadow footwork without racquet swings; this does not constitute clearance to play.

photo.note: Gentle short-court hitting; only if cleared

exercises.name: Standing ankle rocks
exercises.how: In a staggered stance facing a wall, gently bring the front knee forwards over the toes while keeping the heel on the floor. Return and repeat, then change legs.
exercises.watch: Do not force a painful ankle range or collapse the arch.
exercises.why: Gentle ankle preparation for tennis footwork and desk breaks.
exercises.alternatives: E20 calf raises.

photo.note: Ankle dorsiflexion position; photograph kneels, perform standing as described

exercises.name: Gentle seated upper-back rotation
exercises.how: Sit tall with feet supported and arms loosely crossed in front of chest. Turn the upper chest a small amount to one side, then to the other, keeping head and pelvis comfortable.
exercises.watch: Avoid yanking the shoulders, forced spinal twists or painful lower-back rotation.
exercises.why: Small movement after prolonged static posture.
exercises.alternatives: E01 walking; E34 chair-supported upper-back extension.

exercises.name: Calm natural breathing
exercises.how: Sit or stand comfortably. Breathe quietly and naturally, with a relaxed exhale, allowing the shoulders and jaw to release tension. Do not aim for maximal breaths.
exercises.watch: Never hold the breath, hyperventilate or continue if dizzy.
exercises.why: Simple transition from exertion to rest; not a treatment for spinal pain.
exercises.alternatives: Easy walking at a reduced pace.

exercises.name: Gentle forearm extensor stretch
exercises.how: Extend one arm in front with elbow comfortably straight and palm down. With the other hand, gently guide the wrist/fingers downwards until a mild stretch appears on top of the forearm. Switch sides.
exercises.watch: Very light pressure; stop for tingling, wrist pain or nerve-like symptoms.
exercises.why: Optional after gripping a tennis racquet.
exercises.alternatives: Open and close the hands slowly.

exercises.name: Supported quadriceps stretch
exercises.how: Hold a support, bend one knee and bring the heel back slightly. Hold the ankle only if the shoulder reaches comfortably; otherwise use a strap or skip. Keep thighs approximately aligned, pelvis neutral and back upright.
exercises.watch: Do not pull forcefully, arch the back or reach awkwardly with the frozen shoulder.
exercises.why: Optional front-thigh stretch after tennis/gym.
exercises.alternatives: Short, comfortable standing hip flexor stretch E11 (different emphasis).

exercises.name: Band external shoulder rotation
exercises.how: With elbow tucked gently beside body and bent to 90 degrees, rotate hand outwards through a short controlled range against very light band resistance. Return slowly; keep shoulder and neck relaxed.
exercises.watch: Frozen-shoulder pain, neck strain, shrugging or use of a heavy band. Do not perform until approved.
exercises.why: Potential shoulder capacity work for tennis once medically appropriate.
exercises.alternatives: Clinician-approved shoulder rehabilitation work, or E07 without resistance.

photo.note: Band shoulder external rotation; clinician review first

exercises.name: Gentle cross-body shoulder stretch
exercises.how: Bring the affected upper arm gently across the front of the chest. Support at the *upper arm* with the other hand; hold only a mild, approved pull.
exercises.watch: No pressure on the elbow, strong pulling or shoulder pain.
exercises.why: A standard shoulder mobility option, gated for the current frozen-shoulder history.
exercises.alternatives: E08 pendulum.

photo.note: Cross-body shoulder stretch; clinician review first

exercises.name: Bird dog, small-range
exercises.how: From hands and knees with a neutral neck, reach one leg slowly backwards; only add the opposite arm if both shoulder and neck comfortably tolerate it and the physio approves. Keep hips level and movement small.
exercises.watch: This places load through the arms and neck; currently **not part of the default strength routine**. No high leg lifts, twisting or sagging.
exercises.why: A future progression for trunk control, not required now.
exercises.alternatives: E16 supine abdominal march.

photo.note: Full bird dog shown; only small-range clinician-approved version

exercises.name: Chair-supported upper-back extension
exercises.how: Sit upright with hands loosely crossed in front. Gently lift the upper chest a little against the chair back, then return to neutral. Look straight ahead rather than throwing the head backwards.
exercises.watch: Avoid strong lower-back extension, neck extension or pain.
exercises.why: Optional posture variation when working at a desk.
exercises.alternatives: E27 seated upper-back rotation or E01 walking.

photo.note: Chair-supported thoracic extension; do not extend neck

exercises.name: Light rehearsal sets for an already-approved gym lift
exercises.defaultDose: 1-2 sets of 6-8 easy reps at much less than working intensity.
exercises.how: For an exercise **already cleared by the treating clinician**, rehearse the exact movement at very light resistance or without external weight. Increase load only within a programme approved for the current neck/back/shoulder status.
exercises.watch: Never use this to trial a restricted movement (including chest press while prohibited); avoid breath-holding, neck bracing and pain. The website must not supply default working weights.
exercises.why: Progress from general warm-up to the permitted specific gym movement.
exercises.alternatives: Skip this step if there are no cleared lifts to perform.

photo.note: Illustrative example only: a biceps curl, not a prescribed gym lift

exercises.name: Supported standing hamstring stretch
exercises.equipment: Low step or wall/rail for balance
exercises.how: Place one heel slightly in front of you, heel resting on the ground or a low stable step. Keep a slight bend in that knee and hinge forward only a little from the hips with the back comfortably neutral until a mild stretch is felt behind the thigh. Use a wall/rail for balance.
exercises.watch: No deep rounding, bouncing, high leg support or forced straight knee. Stop for radiating pain, tingling or increased back symptoms.
exercises.why: A convenient *optional* alternative to the supine hamstring stretch when a tennis court or gym has no mat.
exercises.alternatives: E13 supine stretch where practical, or skip.

photo.note: Standing heel-on-step hamstring stretch; keep hinge shallow

exercises.name: Gentle neck side tilt (no hand pressure)
exercises.defaultDose: 2 slow tilts per side, with a 1-2-second pause.
exercises.how: Sit tall, relax both shoulders and slowly tip your right ear a short distance towards the right shoulder without rotating the head. Return to centre; repeat left. Stop at a mild, comfortable stretch.
exercises.watch: Do not use the hand to pull the head, lift the shoulder towards the ear, or force a long stretch. Stop for dizziness, headache, numbness or arm symptoms.
exercises.why: Gentle, optional movement for the side of the neck, as included in NHS neck mobility guidance.
exercises.alternatives: E06 gentle neck rotations or E01 walking.

photo.note: Short, hands-free neck side tilt only
